content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate during sentiment downturns (sentiment < 0.4) — model is too conservative, fails to capture rebound potential.
- Lag in price response: model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust downward when sentiment cools.
- Overshoot after spikes: model forecasts peak prices too high after sentiment surges, then undercorrects.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in the first 10 days, then converge — adjust downward early in horizon.
- Sentiment correlation: when sentiment rises > 0.7, model should be 5–10% higher than historical mean; when sentiment drops < 0.3, model should be 5–10% lower.
